tools.name: list_available_accounts
tools.description: List configured accounts as stable non-secret capability records. Use only accounts with can_receive=true for mail reads and can_send=true for send_email and forward_email. If the result is empty, ask the user to run `mcp-email-server ui` or the user-operated CLI; never ask for credentials in chat.

AvailableAccount.description: Stable non-secret capabilities for one account exposed to agents.
AvailableAccount.title: AvailableAccount

tools.name: list_emails_metadata
tools.description: List email metadata (email_id, subject, sender, recipients, date) without body content. Returns email_id for use with get_emails_content.

account_name.description: The name of the email account.
account_name.title: Account Name

page.description: The page number to retrieve (starting from 1).
page.title: Page

page_size.description: The number of emails to retrieve per page.
page_size.title: Page Size

order.description: Sort matching emails by date: oldest first (`asc`) or newest first (`desc`).
order.title: Order

seen.description: Filter by read status: True=read, False=unread, None=all.
seen.title: Seen

flagged.description: Filter by flagged/starred status: True=flagged, False=unflagged, None=all.
flagged.title: Flagged

answered.description: Filter by replied status: True=replied, False=not replied, None=all.
answered.title: Answered

body.description: Search for text in the email body (IMAP BODY).
body.title: Body

text.description: Search for text in the entire message — headers and body (IMAP TEXT).
text.title: Text

has_attachment.description: Filter by attachment presence: True=has attachment, False=none, None=all (multipart/mixed heuristic; may miss inline images or yield false positives).
has_attachment.title: Has Attachment

tools.name: get_emails_content
tools.description: Get the full content (including body and reply-thread headers) of one or more emails by their email_id. Use list_emails_metadata first. This tool is non-read-only because mark_as_read=true changes remote flags.

account_name.description: The name of the email account.
account_name.title: Account Name

email_ids.description: One or more email_id values to retrieve, supplied as an array (obtained from list_emails_metadata).
email_ids.title: Email Ids

mailbox.description: The mailbox to retrieve emails from.
mailbox.title: Mailbox

mark_as_read.description: If True, mark each successfully retrieved email as read. If marking fails, a warning is logged and retrieval still succeeds.
mark_as_read.title: Mark As Read

body_offset.description: Character offset into each email body to start reading from. Use together with max_body_length to page through long emails: if a returned body ends with the '...[TRUNCATED]' marker, fetch the next chunk with body_offset += max_body_length.
body_offset.title: Body Offset

max_body_length.description: Maximum number of body characters to return, counted from body_offset. If the body extends past this window, the '...[TRUNCATED]' marker is appended after the requested body window.
max_body_length.title: Max Body Length

EmailBodyResponse.description: Single email body response with body content and reply-thread headers.
EmailBodyResponse.title: EmailBodyResponse

outputSchema.description: Batch content, optionally handed off as a private local JSON artifact.
outputSchema.title: EmailContentBatchResponse

tools.name: list_allowed_recipients
tools.description: List the configured recipient allowlist — the addresses that send_email and forward_email are permitted to send to and save_to_mailbox is permitted to address. Returns an empty list when unrestricted.

tools.name: list_allowed_senders
tools.description: List the configured inbound sender allowlist — the address patterns whose mail the server will read or act on. When configured, only these senders' mail is visible to the read tools (list_emails_metadata, get_emails_content, download_attachment, and forward_email's source read) and eligible for the mutation tools (delete_emails, set_email_flags, mark_emails_as_read, move_emails, archive_emails). Returns an empty list when unrestricted.

tools.name: send_email
tools.description: Send one email using the specified account. Supports reply threading. Partial or ambiguous SMTP delivery reports per-recipient succeeded/failed/unknown status and reports the independent Sent-copy outcome separately; ambiguous effects are not retried automatically.

account_name.description: The name of the email account to send from.
account_name.title: Account Name

recipients.description: A list of recipient email addresses.
recipients.title: Recipients

cc.description: A list of CC email addresses.
cc.title: Cc

bcc.description: A list of BCC email addresses.
bcc.title: Bcc

html.description: Whether to send the email as HTML (True) or plain text (False).
html.title: Html

attachments.description: A list of file paths to attach. Relative paths are resolved against the server process working directory; absolute paths are recommended.
attachments.title: Attachments

in_reply_to.description: Message-ID of the email being replied to. Enables proper threading in email clients.
in_reply_to.title: In Reply To

references.description: Space-separated Message-IDs for the thread chain. Usually includes in_reply_to plus ancestors.
references.title: References

reply_to.description: Email address to set as the Reply-To header. When set, email clients will reply to this address instead of the From address.
reply_to.title: Reply To

tools.name: forward_email
tools.description: Forward an existing message to new recipients using the specified account. The source message is read over IMAP first: if it cannot be read, the call fails before any SMTP session is opened, so a forward is never delivered without the content it was supposed to carry. The subject is derived from the source as 'Fwd: <original subject>' without stacking a second prefix, the caller's note is placed above a plain-text forwarded block re-composed from the source's parsed text body, and the source's attachments are re-attached with their original MIME types unless include_attachments is false. Partial or ambiguous SMTP delivery reports per-recipient succeeded/failed/unknown status and reports the independent Sent-copy outcome separately; ambiguous effects are not retried automatically.

account_name.description: The name of the email account to forward from.
account_name.title: Account Name

email_id.description: UID of the source message to forward.
email_id.title: Email Id

recipients.description: A list of addresses that receive the forwarded message.
recipients.title: Recipients

source_mailbox.description: The mailbox that contains the source message.
source_mailbox.title: Source Mailbox

body.description: An optional note placed above the forwarded content.
body.title: Body

cc.description: A list of CC email addresses.
cc.title: Cc

bcc.description: A list of BCC email addresses.
bcc.title: Bcc

include_attachments.description: Whether to re-attach the source message's attachments.
include_attachments.title: Include Attachments

tools.name: save_to_mailbox
tools.description: Compose an email and save it to an IMAP folder (e.g., Drafts). Shares recipient, body, attachment, and threading parameters with send_email; adds mailbox and flags, and does not support reply_to. Default folder is Drafts with \Draft and \Seen flags. Pure IMAP operation — works without SMTP configuration. An ambiguous APPEND is reported as unknown and is not retried automatically.

account_name.description: The name of the email account.
account_name.title: Account Name

recipients.description: A list of recipient email addresses.
recipients.title: Recipients

mailbox.description: The IMAP folder to save to (e.g., 'Drafts', 'INBOX.Drafts', 'Templates').
mailbox.title: Mailbox

cc.description: A list of CC email addresses.
cc.title: Cc

bcc.description: A list of BCC email addresses.
bcc.title: Bcc

html.description: Whether the email body is HTML (True) or plain text (False).
html.title: Html

attachments.description: A list of file paths to attach. Relative paths are resolved against the server process working directory; absolute paths are recommended.
attachments.title: Attachments

in_reply_to.description: Message-ID of the email being replied to. Enables proper threading in email clients.
in_reply_to.title: In Reply To

references.description: Space-separated Message-IDs for the thread chain.
references.title: References

flags.description: IMAP flags to set on the message. Defaults to ['\Draft', '\Seen']. Common flags: '\Draft', '\Seen', '\Flagged'.
flags.title: Flags

tools.name: delete_emails
tools.description: Delete one or more emails by email_id using target-scoped UID EXPUNGE. Use list_emails_metadata first. Partial or ambiguous effects report per-ID succeeded/failed/unknown status and are not retried automatically.

account_name.description: The name of the email account.
account_name.title: Account Name

email_ids.description: List of email_id to delete (obtained from list_emails_metadata).
email_ids.title: Email Ids

mailbox.description: The mailbox to delete emails from.
mailbox.title: Mailbox

tools.name: set_email_flags
tools.description: Add or remove approved IMAP flags on one or more emails by email_id. Supported flags are \Seen, \Flagged, \Answered, and \Draft; \Deleted and provider-specific keywords are not supported. Use list_emails_metadata first. Partial or ambiguous effects report per-ID succeeded/failed/unknown status and are not retried automatically.

account_name.description: The name of the email account.
account_name.title: Account Name

email_ids.description: List of email_id values whose flags should be changed.
email_ids.title: Email Ids

operation.description: Whether to add or remove every supplied flag.
operation.title: Operation

flags.description: Unique approved flags to add or remove: \Seen, \Flagged, \Answered, or \Draft.
flags.title: Flags

tools.name: mark_emails_as_read
tools.description: Mark one or more emails as read by email_id. This is the common-workflow equivalent of adding \Seen with set_email_flags. Use list_emails_metadata first. Partial or ambiguous effects report per-ID succeeded/failed/unknown status and are not retried automatically.

account_name.description: The name of the email account.
account_name.title: Account Name

email_ids.description: List of email_id to mark as read (obtained from list_emails_metadata).
email_ids.title: Email Ids

tools.name: move_emails
tools.description: Move one or more emails between IMAP folders by email_id. Use list_emails_metadata and list_mailboxes first. Partial or ambiguous effects report per-ID succeeded/failed/unknown status and are not retried.

account_name.description: The name of the email account.
account_name.title: Account Name

email_ids.description: List of email_id to move (obtained from list_emails_metadata).
email_ids.title: Email Ids

destination_mailbox.description: The destination mailbox/folder to move emails to.
destination_mailbox.title: Destination Mailbox

source_mailbox.description: The source mailbox containing the emails.
source_mailbox.title: Source Mailbox

tools.name: archive_emails
tools.description: Archive one or more emails by moving them to the account's Archive folder, auto-detected via the RFC 6154 \Archive flag (falling back to common names like Archive or [Gmail]/All Mail). Use list_emails_metadata first. Partial or ambiguous effects report per-ID succeeded/failed/unknown status and are not retried automatically.

account_name.description: The name of the email account.
account_name.title: Account Name

email_ids.description: List of email_id to archive (obtained from list_emails_metadata).
email_ids.title: Email Ids

mailbox.description: The source mailbox containing the emails.
mailbox.title: Mailbox

tools.name: list_mailboxes
tools.description: List available mailboxes/folders for an email account. Returns folder names, hierarchy delimiters, and flags. Useful for discovering folder names before moving emails.

account_name.description: The name of the email account.
account_name.title: Account Name

pattern.description: IMAP LIST pattern. Use '*' for all folders, 'INBOX.*' for INBOX children.
pattern.title: Pattern

reference.description: IMAP LIST reference name (namespace prefix). Usually empty.
reference.title: Reference

tools.name: download_attachment
tools.description: Download an email attachment. By default it is saved with a safe randomized name under the current user's Downloads/mcp-email-server directory; an explicit destination path remains supported. This feature must be explicitly enabled in settings (enable_attachment_download=true) due to security considerations.

account_name.description: The name of the email account.
account_name.title: Account Name

email_id.description: The email ID (obtained from list_emails_metadata or get_emails_content).
email_id.title: Email Id

attachment_name.description: The name of the attachment to download (as shown in the attachments list).
attachment_name.title: Attachment Name

save_path.description: Optional exact destination path. Omit it to use a safe randomized filename under the current user's Downloads/mcp-email-server directory. Relative explicit paths are resolved against the server process working directory.
save_path.title: Save Path

mailbox.description: The mailbox to search in (default: INBOX).
mailbox.title: Mailbox

resource_templates.name: get_account
resource_templates.description: Return stable non-secret discovery capabilities for one configured account.
